theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is the main danger when a person touches a live conductor?
options: They may feel a small static spark that does no harm
Their tools may become blunt and need sharpening sooner
Current may flow through their body and shock them
The cable insulation may slowly turn a darker colour

questions.stem: A worn extension lead has bare copper showing near the plug. What hazard does this create?
options: Electric shock, or a fire if the bare copper shorts
The lead will draw less power, so tools run slowly
The plug will fit too loosely in the socket outlet
The lead will become too stiff to roll up and store

questions.stem: What is an arc flash?
options: A light on a tester that shows its battery is low
The glow of a lamp at the moment it is switched on
A static spark that jumps from a nylon shirt on a dry day
A blast of heat and light from a fault between conductors

questions.stem: Why is a socket outlet with many adaptors plugged into it dangerous?
options: It makes the meter run backwards and read wrong
Too much current can overheat it and start a fire
All the appliances will switch off every hour
The voltage at the outlet rises far above normal

questions.stem: Which of these places has the greatest risk of electric shock?
options: A dry office with plastic floor tiles
A wet floor beside a water pump and its cable
A storeroom with wooden shelves and a dry floor
A classroom with all the lights switched off

questions.stem: Which of these is a sign that a cable or fitting is overheating?
options: The cable is neatly clipped along the wall
The socket cover is clean and bright white
The breaker labels are clear and easy to read
A burning smell and brown marks around it

questions.stem: Which path of current through the body is the most dangerous?
options: From one hand to the other, across the chest
From one finger to the next on the same hand
Along the skin of one forearm, wrist to elbow
From the heel to the toes of the same foot

questions.stem: Why can a shock make a person unable to let go of a live conductor?
options: The rubber soles of their shoes melt and hold them down
The cable becomes a magnet and pulls the hand towards it
The current makes the muscles of the hand clench tight
The heat of the conductor glues the skin to the metal

questions.stem: Why is a shock more dangerous when a person's skin is wet?
options: Wet skin lets more current flow into the body
Wet skin makes the supply voltage go much higher
Wet skin changes the supply from AC to DC
Wet skin makes the breaker slower to reset

questions.stem: Besides the shock itself, which injury is common in electrical accidents?
options: Eye strain from looking closely at the cable colours
Hearing loss from the click of a light switch
Burns where the current enters and leaves the body
Sunburn from working under the workshop lamps

questions.stem: You have found which breaker feeds the socket outlet you will work on. What do you do next?
options: Prove the outlet dead with a voltage tester
Switch that breaker off at the distribution board
Remove the cover of the socket outlet to look inside
Tell the customer the work will take one hour

questions.stem: Why do you fit your own padlock to a breaker or isolator after switching it off?
options: To show the supervisor which breaker is the newest
To stop the breaker from tripping while you work
To keep the breaker cool while the circuit is off
So nobody else can switch it on while you work

questions.stem: What should a danger tag on a locked-off breaker show?
options: The price of the breaker and the shop it came from
The date the board was first put in the building
The size of the cable that the breaker protects
Who isolated it, the date, and the work being done

questions.stem: Who should remove a lock and tag from an isolated circuit?
options: Any worker who needs that circuit switched back on
The person who fitted it, when their work is done
The building owner, as soon as they come on site
The first person to arrive at work the next day

questions.stem: Why must you test that a circuit is dead even after you have switched it off?
options: Testing makes the breaker switch off more firmly
Testing drains any charge left in the cable to earth
The wrong breaker may be off, or a label may be wrong
Testing is needed on 110 V circuits, but not on 220 V

questions.stem: Before you use a voltage tester to prove a circuit dead, what must you do?
options: Check that the tester works on a known live source
Check that the tester has brand-new test leads
Check that the tester is the same colour as the board
Check that the tester was switched off overnight

questions.stem: After you prove a circuit dead, why do you check the tester again on the known live source?
options: To use up the battery before it goes flat by itself
To make sure the tester did not fail during the test
To warm the probes so that the next test is quicker
To show the customer that the supply is back on

questions.stem: What is a proving unit used for?
options: To give a known voltage so you can check a tester works
To measure how much power a building uses each month
To switch off all the circuits in a board at one time
To find where a cable runs inside a concrete wall

questions.stem: Which is the correct order for safe isolation?
options: Prove dead, check tester, switch off, lock off and tag, check tester
Lock off and tag, check tester, switch off, check tester, prove dead
Switch off, lock off and tag, check tester, prove dead, check tester
Check tester, switch off, prove dead, check tester, lock off and tag

questions.stem: Which is the best device for proving a circuit dead?
options: A screwdriver with a neon lamp in the handle
A table lamp plugged into the socket outlet
A quick touch on the wires with the back of the hand
A two-pole voltage tester made for the job

questions.stem: Why is a neon test screwdriver a poor choice for proving a circuit dead?
options: It is too small and gets lost in most tool bags
It works only on circuits that are 220 V
It may not light up, and so give a false dead result
It makes the circuit breaker trip every time it is used

questions.stem: When you prove a 110 V socket outlet dead, between which conductors should you test?
options: Between line and neutral, and nothing else
Between line and earth, and nothing else
Between neutral and earth, and nothing else
Line to neutral, line to earth, neutral to earth

questions.stem: What is the main job of a fuse or a circuit breaker?
options: To cut off the supply when too much current flows
To raise the voltage when many appliances are on
To measure the energy used for the power bill
To change the supply from AC to DC for appliances

questions.stem: What does a residual current device (RCD), also called a GFCI, do?
options: It lowers the voltage so that a shock is not felt
It trips when it senses current leaking to earth
It stores power to keep lights on in a blackout
It counts how many times the circuit is switched on

questions.stem: How should a user check that an RCD (GFCI) is working?
options: Press its test button and see that it trips
Touch a live wire to see if it switches off
Look to see that the case is free of dust
Switch every appliance on at the same time

questions.stem: Why is the metal case of an appliance connected to earth?
options: So that the appliance uses less power each day
So fault current flows away and the breaker trips
So that the metal case does not rust in damp weather
So the appliance can plug into any type of outlet

questions.stem: A breaker trips each time a heater is switched on. What should you do?
options: Hold the breaker lever up so that it cannot trip
Fit a bigger breaker so that it stops tripping
Wrap tape around the breaker to keep it on
Stop using the heater and report it for checking

questions.stem: Which footwear is best for electrical work?
options: Open sandals, so that the feet stay cool and dry
Boots with metal studs on the soles, for good grip
Safety boots with insulating soles, kept dry
Soft canvas shoes, so you can feel the floor

questions.stem: What does it mean when a screwdriver is insulated and marked with a voltage rating?
options: It is safe to use on live circuits at any time
It can be used as a tester to find live conductors
It will never wear out, so it needs no checks
It gives extra protection, but you still work dead

questions.stem: You find a crack in the insulated handle of your pliers. What should you do?
options: Wrap the crack in insulating tape and keep using them
Use them only on 110 V circuits from now on
Take them out of use and replace them
Paint over the crack so that water cannot get in

questions.stem: Why should you take off rings, watches and metal chains before electrical work?
options: So they are not scratched by the tools and cables
Metal jewellery can conduct current and cause burns
So the tester gives a more accurate reading
So that you can work faster without them on

questions.stem: Before you use an electric drill, what should you check?
options: The cord, plug and casing for any damage
That the cord is long enough to reach the roof
That the chuck key is taped to the cord
That the plug is still warm from its last use

questions.stem: An extension lead is on a drum (reel). Why should it be fully unwound for a heavy load?
options: So that it is easier for others to see on the floor
A coiled lead can overheat when a large current flows
So that the voltage goes up at the far end of the lead
So that the plug on the drum does not get lost

questions.stem: What does a symbol of a square inside a square on a power tool mean?
options: The tool must always be used with an earth wire
The tool is waterproof and can be used in rain
The tool can only be used on a 220 V supply
The tool is double insulated

questions.stem: You must use a power tool outdoors where the ground is damp. What is the safest way?
options: Use an RCD-protected supply and keep the lead off wet ground
Stand on a metal sheet so that you do not touch the soil
Work as fast as you can before the ground gets any wetter
Wrap the plug and socket in a plastic bag to keep them dry

questions.stem: Ricardo must carry a long aluminium ladder near overhead power lines. What should he do?
options: Carry it upright so that he can see where it goes
Touch the line quickly with the ladder to test it
Keep the ladder low and well away from the lines
Ask someone to lift the line up out of the way

questions.stem: Which ladder is best for electrical work?
options: An aluminium ladder, because it is light to carry
A steel ladder, because it is strong and stiff
A fibreglass ladder, because it does not conduct
Any ladder at all, as long as it is tall enough

questions.stem: When you climb a ladder, how many points of contact should you keep?
options: Three, such as two feet and one hand
One, so that both hands are free
Two, with both feet on the same rung
Four, but only on short ladders

questions.stem: Which extinguisher is suitable for a fire in electrical equipment?
options: A water extinguisher, held well back
A foam extinguisher, aimed at the base
A bucket of wet sand thrown over it
A carbon dioxide (CO2) extinguisher

questions.stem: A small fire starts in a distribution board. If it is safe to do so, what should you do first?
options: Throw water on it to cool it down quickly
Raise the alarm and switch off the supply
Open the board cover to see where it started
Carry on working until it goes out by itself

questions.stem: Why must you never use water on an electrical fire?
options: Water conducts and can give the user a shock
Water makes the smoke smell much stronger
Water spreads the heat to the next room
Water will rust the extinguisher on the wall

questions.stem: Your co-worker Andre is still touching a live cable after a shock. What do you do first?
options: Grab his arm firmly and pull him away from the cable
Switch off the supply, or push him clear with dry wood
Pour water over him to cool down the burns
Run to find his supervisor before doing anything

questions.stem: Once a shock casualty is free of the supply, what should you do next?
options: Give them a cold drink and send them home
Leave them alone so that they can rest quietly
Call for medical help and check their breathing
Ask them to stand up and walk it off at once

questions.stem: Why should a person who had an electric shock see a doctor even if they feel fine?
options: They may need a new pair of safety boots
The doctor must sign their timesheet before they go home
The shock may have changed their blood group
The shock may have harmed the heart or burned inside

questions.stem: After an electrical accident or a near miss at the Centre, what must you do?
options: Keep quiet so that nobody gets into trouble
Tell only your friends about it at break time
Wait to see if it happens again before you say anything at all
Report it to your supervisor and fill in the report form

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What do the letters LOTO stand for in safe isolation?
What is the general name for the switch used to cut off all supply to a circuit or machine so that work can be done safely?
Which organ of the body is most at risk when current flows across the chest?
What do we call a material, such as rubber, plastic or dry wood, that does not let current flow through it easily?
What do we call a material, such as copper, that lets current flow through it easily?
What are the letters for the emergency first aid, given by a trained person, that pushes on the chest and gives rescue breaths when the heart has stopped?
What do we call an event that could have caused an injury but did not, and that must still be reported?
Apart from carbon dioxide (CO2), which type of extinguisher is also suitable for fires in electrical equipment?
Into which position should you place a casualty who is unconscious but breathing, while you wait for help?
What is the name of the conductor that connects the metal case of an appliance to earth?
When you unplug an appliance, which part should you hold and pull, instead of the cord?
What is the word for joining metal parts, such as water pipes and steel frames, with a conductor so that they stay at the same voltage?
What is the name of the card or plastic label that you fix to a locked-off isolator to warn others?
What is the name of the written check, done before a job starts, that lists the hazards of the task and how to control them?
What do we call it when a circuit carries more current than it was made to carry, for example from too many appliances?

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would safely isolate a socket-outlet circuit before working on it.
essays.modelAnswer: First I check the circuit chart and find the breaker or isolator that feeds the outlet, and I tell anyone affected that the power will be off. I switch the breaker off. I then lock it off with my own padlock, using a lockout device or hasp, and keep the only key in my pocket. I fix a danger tag that shows my name, the date and the work being done. Next I check my two-pole voltage tester on a proving unit or a known live source to make sure it works. I then test at the outlet between line and neutral, line and earth, and neutral and earth, and see no voltage. I check the tester again on the proving unit to be sure it did not fail during the test. Only then do I treat the circuit as dead and start work. I never work on a circuit that is live.
markingPoints: Identifies the correct circuit and switches it off at the breaker or isolator
Locks it off with a personal lock and keeps the key
Fixes a tag with name, date and the work
Checks the tester on a proving unit or known live source before and after testing
Proves dead between all conductors (L-N, L-E, N-E) before touching anything; never works live

essays.stem: A worker in the workshop has had an electric shock and is still touching the faulty equipment. Explain what you would do to help them, in the right order.
essays.modelAnswer: First I must not touch the person, because the current could pass into me as well. I shout for help and switch off the supply at the plug, switch or breaker as quickly as I can. If I cannot switch it off, I stand on something dry, such as a wooden board or a rubber mat, and push the person or the cable away with a dry piece of wood or another non-conducting object. Once they are free, I or someone else calls for medical help straight away. I check whether they are responding and breathing. If they are breathing but unconscious, I put them in the recovery position. If they are not breathing, a trained first-aider starts CPR and keeps going until help arrives. I cover burns with a clean, dry dressing. Even if they say they feel fine, they must see a doctor, because a shock can harm the heart.
markingPoints: Does not touch the casualty while they are still in contact with the supply
Switches off the supply, or separates them with a dry non-conducting object while standing on dry insulation
Calls for medical help at once
Checks response and breathing; recovery position, or CPR by a trained person if not breathing
Treats burns with a clean dry dressing and sends the casualty for a medical check

essays.stem: Explain what happens to the body during an electric shock and describe what makes a shock more serious.
essays.modelAnswer: In an electric shock, current flows through the body because the person has become part of a circuit, for example between a live part and earth. The current makes the muscles tighten, so a person may not be able to let go of the conductor. Current through the chest can upset the rhythm of the heart and stop it pumping properly, and it can stop breathing. The current also heats the body and causes burns, often deep ones, where it goes in and comes out. A shock can also make a person fall from a ladder. A shock is more serious when the current is larger, when it flows for a longer time, and when its path crosses the heart, such as from hand to hand or hand to foot. Wet skin, wet floors and bare feet lower the body's resistance and let more current flow, so the shock is worse.
markingPoints: Current flows through the body when it becomes part of a circuit (for example live to earth)
Muscles tighten, so the person may not be able to let go
Current can stop the heart or breathing, and causes burns at entry and exit points
Worse with more current, longer time, or a path across the heart
Water or wet conditions lower resistance and increase the current

essays.stem: Name four electrical hazards that may be found in a training workshop and say how each one can be controlled.
essays.modelAnswer: Damaged cords and plugs, with cracked insulation or bare wires, can cause shock or fire. They are controlled by checking every lead before use and taking damaged ones out of use with a tag. Overloaded socket outlets, with many adaptors, can overheat and start a fire, so each heavy appliance should have its own outlet and adaptors should not be stacked. Water near electrical equipment, such as a leaking roof or a mopped floor, increases the risk of shock, so equipment should be kept dry and supplied through RCD (GFCI) protection. Circuits that are switched on by mistake while someone works on them are controlled by safe isolation, with lock off, tag and prove dead. Exposed live parts, such as a board with its cover off, must be covered or barriered and kept closed. Any hazard that cannot be fixed at once is reported to the instructor.
markingPoints: Names at least four real electrical hazards (damaged leads, overload, water, exposed live parts, unexpected switching on)
Gives a suitable control for damaged leads (check before use, tag out)
Gives a suitable control for overload or water (own outlet, keep dry, RCD protection)
Includes safe isolation or covering live parts as a control
Says hazards that cannot be fixed are reported

essays.stem: Explain how earthing, circuit breakers and RCDs (GFCIs) work together to protect people from electric shock and fire.
essays.modelAnswer: Earthing connects the metal parts of equipment, such as the case of a washing machine, to earth with a protective conductor. If a live wire touches the metal case, a large fault current flows through the earth conductor instead of through a person. This large current makes the fuse or circuit breaker operate quickly and cut off the supply, so the case does not stay live. A breaker also protects the cable by tripping when the circuit is overloaded or has a short circuit, which stops the cable overheating and starting a fire. An RCD, also called a GFCI, compares the current going out on the line with the current coming back on the neutral. If some current leaks to earth, for example through a person, it trips very fast, before the shock can do serious harm. It should be tested often with its test button.
markingPoints: Earthing gives fault current a path away from people through the protective conductor
Fault current makes the fuse or breaker cut off the supply quickly
Breakers and fuses stop overload and short circuits overheating cables and causing fire
An RCD (GFCI) senses current leaking to earth, such as through a person, and trips fast
The RCD is checked often with its test button

essays.stem: Describe how you would check a portable power tool and its extension lead before use, and what you would do if you found a fault.
essays.modelAnswer: Before I plug in, I look along the whole cord of the tool and the extension lead for cuts, cracks, burns or tape repairs, and I check that the outer sheath goes fully into the plug and the tool. I look at the plug for cracks, loose or bent pins and burn marks. I check the casing of the tool for cracks and make sure the guard and switch work properly. I check that the extension lead is the right rating for the tool and that I will unwind a drum fully. I make sure I will use an RCD-protected supply. If I find any fault, I do not use the tool or lead. I unplug it, fix a 'Do not use' tag to it with the fault and the date, put it aside where nobody will pick it up, and report it to my instructor for repair or replacement.
markingPoints: Checks the cord along its full length for damage and that the sheath is gripped at both ends
Checks the plug and the tool casing, guard and switch
Checks the extension lead rating, unwinds drums, and uses an RCD-protected supply
Does not use faulty equipment: unplugs it and tags it
Takes it out of use and reports it

essays.stem: Explain how electrical fires can be prevented, and what you should do if an electrical fire starts.
essays.modelAnswer: Electrical fires can be prevented by not overloading socket outlets, by using the right size of cable and breaker for each circuit, and by never bypassing or taping up a breaker that keeps tripping. Damaged cords and loose connections should be repaired by a competent person, because they can get hot and spark. Flammable materials, such as paper and rags, should be kept away from boards, heaters and lamps, and leads should not be run under rugs. If a fire starts, I raise the alarm and tell everyone to leave. If it is safe, I switch off the supply at the main switch or breaker. Only if the fire is small and I have been trained do I use a carbon dioxide or dry powder extinguisher, keeping my escape route behind me. I never use water. If the fire grows, I leave, close the door and call the fire service.
markingPoints: Prevention: no overloading; correct cable and breaker size; never bypass a tripping breaker
Prevention: repair damaged cords and loose connections; keep flammables away
Raises the alarm and switches off the supply if safe
Uses only CO2 or dry powder on a small fire, never water, with an escape route
Leaves and calls the fire service if the fire grows

essays.stem: Describe the PPE and insulated tools an electrician uses, and explain why they do not make it safe to work on live circuits.
essays.modelAnswer: An electrician wears safety boots with insulating soles to protect the feet and to reduce the chance of current passing through to the ground. Safety glasses protect the eyes from dust when drilling and from flying pieces of wire when cutting. Gloves protect the hands from cuts. A hard hat is worn where things may fall. Clothing should be cotton and fit well, and rings, watches and chains are removed because metal conducts. Insulated screwdrivers and pliers, marked with a voltage rating, give an extra layer of protection if a conductor is live by mistake. However, PPE and insulated tools can be damaged or worn, and a slip can still bring a hand or arm onto a live part. They are a last line of defence, not a safe way of working. The safe way is always to isolate the circuit, lock it off, tag it and prove it dead before work.
markingPoints: Names suitable PPE: insulating-soled boots, safety glasses, gloves, hard hat where needed
Removes metal jewellery and wears suitable clothing
Insulated tools with a voltage rating give extra protection against accidental contact
Explains that PPE and tools can fail or be worn, and a slip can still cause contact
States that the safe method is always isolation and proving dead, never working live

essays.stem: Explain how you would work safely with electricity outdoors in the rainy season, including near overhead power lines.
essays.modelAnswer: Rain and wet ground make electric shock much more likely, because water lowers the body's resistance and can carry current. I would not use mains power tools in the rain. Where I must use them outdoors, I use an RCD-protected supply, or battery tools, and I keep plugs, sockets and leads off wet ground and out of puddles. I use equipment marked as suitable for outdoor use, and I keep my hands, gloves and boots dry. If water gets into a tool or lead, I stop, unplug it and have it checked. Near overhead power lines, I look up and plan the job before starting. I keep ladders, scaffold poles and long tools low and well away from the lines, and I use non-conducting ladders. I never touch a fallen line, and I keep other people away from it. I report any fallen or low line to the power company and the supervisor.
markingPoints: Explains that water increases the risk of shock
Avoids mains tools in rain; uses RCD protection or battery tools; keeps leads and plugs off wet ground
Keeps hands, PPE and equipment dry; stops and checks equipment that gets wet
Looks up and keeps ladders and long items well away from overhead lines
Never touches a fallen line, keeps people away and reports it

essays.stem: Explain why accidents, near misses and unsafe conditions must be reported, and say what a good report should include.
essays.modelAnswer: Accidents and near misses must be reported so that the cause can be found and fixed before someone else is hurt. A near miss is a warning: next time the same fault may cause a serious injury. Reports also make sure an injured person gets proper care and that the Centre keeps a true record, which may be needed later. Reporting unsafe conditions, such as a damaged socket outlet or a missing board cover, means the hazard can be repaired and others can be warned. A good report is made as soon as possible to the supervisor or instructor and written on the report form. It should give the date, time and exact place, the names of the people involved and any witnesses, and a clear, honest description of what happened. It should state any injury and the first aid given, the equipment involved, and the action taken to make the area safe.
markingPoints: Reporting lets the cause be found and fixed so others are not hurt
Near misses are warnings of future accidents
Reports ensure care for the injured and keep a true record
Report is made promptly to the supervisor on the correct form
Content: date, time, place, people and witnesses, what happened, injury, first aid and action taken

practical1.title: Safe isolation, lock off and prove dead on a training board circuit
practical1.brief: As a group, carry out the full safe isolation procedure on one socket-outlet circuit of the Centre's training board. The instructor switches the board on, stays with the group throughout and keeps the board cover closed. Every member does the whole procedure once, in turn, while the others watch and check it against the steps on the isolation record sheet: (1) find the circuit on the board chart and tell the group it will be switched off, (2) switch off the breaker or isolator, (3) fit a lockout hasp, then your own padlock, and fix a danger tag with your name, the date and the job, (4) check the two-pole voltage tester on the proving unit, (5) test at the outlet between line and neutral, line and earth, and neutral and earth, and say the result out loud, (6) check the tester again on the proving unit, (7) write your results on the record sheet and sign it. While one member works, every other member must also add their own lock to the hasp, so that the circuit cannot be switched on until all locks are off. At the end, each member removes only their own lock, and only the instructor switches the circuit back on. Nobody removes any cover or touches any conductor during this task. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the record sheet once for the whole group.
materials: The Centre's training board with labelled breakers and a socket-outlet circuit, fed through an RCD (GFCI)
A lockout hasp that takes several padlocks, and a lockout device to fit the breaker
One personal padlock with its own key for each member
Danger tags and a marker pen
A two-pole voltage tester with shrouded probes
A proving unit made for the tester
An isolation record sheet (one for the group)
Safety boots and safety glasses for every member
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The board chart, with the circuit to be isolated marked
The breaker switched off, with the lockout device fitted
The hasp with every member's padlock and a filled-in danger tag
The tester being checked on the proving unit before the test
Proving dead at the outlet, with the tester showing no voltage
The tester being checked on the proving unit after the test
The completed and signed isolation record sheet
checklist: Found the correct circuit from the chart and warned others before switching off
Switched off the correct breaker or isolator
Fitted the lockout device and their own padlock, and kept their key
Filled in a danger tag clearly with name, date and job
Checked the tester on the proving unit before testing
Tested between all three pairs (L-N, L-E, N-E) and read the result correctly
Checked the tester again on the proving unit after testing
Recorded the results and signed the record sheet
Removed only their own lock at the end and did not switch the circuit on
safety: Treat every circuit as live until you have proved it dead with a tester that you checked before and after
Never remove a board cover or touch a conductor in this task; the instructor stays with the group
Use only a two-pole tester with shrouded probes and leads in good condition; do not use a neon screwdriver
Never remove another person's lock or tag, and never switch on a circuit that is locked off
Wear safety boots and glasses, remove metal jewellery, and keep the area dry; follow the maker's instructions and the Centre's rules

practical2.title: Electric shock rescue and first-aid role play, with an incident report
practical2.brief: As a group, act out a rescue from an electric shock and then write it up. The scenario: Kemar, an apprentice, has had a shock from a damaged drill lead in the workshop and is still holding the drill. The drill and lead are NOT connected to any supply: the plug is taped and marked TRAINING, and a training manikin, or a member who agrees to lie still, plays Kemar. Run the role play once for each member, so that every member takes the rescuer's part once while the others play the helper who calls for medical help, the person who checks the area is safe, and the recorder. In each run the rescuer must: (1) shout for help and not touch the casualty, (2) switch off at the socket or breaker, or say how they would push the lead clear with a dry wooden broom handle while standing on a dry board, (3) check response and breathing, (4) put the casualty in the recovery position and say what they would do if he were not breathing, and (5) cover a 'burn' on the hand with a clean dry dressing. Then, as a group, fill in the Centre's incident report form for the event and make a small poster, 'What to do if someone gets a shock', for the workshop wall. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in the report and poster once for the whole group.
materials: A drill with a damaged-looking lead, with the plug taped and marked TRAINING (not connected to any supply)
A dry wooden broom handle and a dry wooden board or rubber mat
A training manikin, or a blanket and mat if a member plays the casualty
A first-aid kit with clean dry dressings
Chart paper and markers for the poster
A phone or camera for the photos
photos: The scene set up, with the TRAINING label on the plug clearly shown
The rescuer switching off at the socket or breaker, without touching the casualty
The rescuer standing on the dry board and showing how to move the lead with the broom handle
The casualty in the recovery position, with the burn dressing in place
checklist: Did not touch the casualty before the supply was off or the casualty was clear
Switched off the supply, or used a dry non-conducting object while standing on dry insulation
Called, or sent someone to call, for medical help straight away
Checked response and breathing, and said correctly when CPR is needed and who gives it
Placed the casualty in the recovery position correctly
Covered the burn with a clean dry dressing, and said the casualty must see a doctor
Gave accurate details for the incident report (time, place, people, what happened, action taken)
Took an active part in making the poster
safety: The training drill must never be plugged in; check that the plug is taped and marked before you start
Be gentle with the person playing the casualty; never do real chest compressions on a person
Keep the floor clear and dry so nobody slips during the role play
In a real event, never touch a shock casualty until the supply is off or they are clear; follow the Centre's first-aid rules
